sub_graphs.name: BPO Hardfork Definition
sub_graphs.description: Defines BPO (Blob Parameter Only) hardforks as protocol upgrades that modify only blob-related parameters through configuration, without requiring any client-side code changes. New parameters take effect immediately at the specified activation time.

invariants.text: BPO hardforks MUST NOT require any client-side code changes; they are configuration-only upgrades.
New blob parameters take effect immediately at the specified activation time.

sub_graphs.name: Blob Schedule Configuration
sub_graphs.description: Defines the three protocol parameters managed by the blob schedule configuration: target (expected blobs per block), max (maximum blobs per block), and baseFeeUpdateFraction (blob gas pricing adjustment factor).

invariants.text: When a regular hardfork changes any blob parameters, it MUST do so by adding an entry to the blob schedule configuration.

state_variables.name: target
state_variables.description: The expected number of blobs per block (Blob Target).

state_variables.name: max
state_variables.description: The maximum number of blobs per block (Blob Limit).

state_variables.name: baseFeeUpdateFraction
state_variables.description: Determines how blob gas pricing adjusts per block (Blob Base Fee Update Fraction).

data_structures.name: BlobSchedule
data_structures.source:
class BlobSchedule:
   target: U64
   max: U64
   base_fee_update_fraction: Uint

sub_graphs.name: Execution Layer Configuration
sub_graphs.description: Specifies how BPO forks are configured on the execution layer. Each fork in the blobSchedule object (defined in EIP-7840) is linked to an activation timestamp via a top-level <fork_name>Time field holding the Unix timestamp as a JSON number. BPO forks use the naming convention bpo<index> starting at 1. Activation timestamps are only required for forks after Prague.

invariants.text: BPO forks SHOULD be named using the convention 'bpo<index>', where <index> starts at 1.
Activation timestamps are required only for forks that occur after Prague.
Since there is no backporting, the values for cancunTime and pragueTime are set to 0.

data_structures.name: EL blobSchedule JSON
data_structures.description: Top-level JSON configuration containing a blobSchedule object mapping fork names to blob parameter objects, plus <fork_name>Time fields for activation timestamps.

sub_graphs.name: Blob Base Fee Computations
sub_graphs.description: Modifies the functions get_base_fee_per_blob_gas and calc_excess_blob_gas (originally from EIP-4844) to explicitly use the blob schedule. The current block's blob schedule is used (consistent with EIP-7691). TARGET_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK is removed and replaced with GAS_PER_BLOB * blob_schedule.target.

invariants.text: TARGET_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK is removed and replaced with GAS_PER_BLOB * blob_schedule.target.
The functions use the current block's blob schedule for computations (consistent with EIP-7691 handling).

functions.description: Calculates excess blob gas for the current block. Computes target_blob_gas as GAS_PER_BLOB * blob_schedule.target. Returns 0 if (parent.excess_blob_gas + parent.blob_gas_used) < target_blob_gas, otherwise returns the difference.

sub_graphs.name: Consensus Layer Configuration
sub_graphs.description: Defines the BLOB_SCHEDULE field in the consensus layer configuration, containing a sequence of entries representing blob parameter changes after ELECTRA_FORK_EPOCH. There is one entry per fork that changes blob parameters, whether regular or BPO.

invariants.text: Execution and consensus clients MUST share consistent BPO fork schedules.
The slot number in the EL's blobSchedule MUST align with the start of the epoch specified in the consensus layer configuration.
The 'max' field in the EL's blobSchedule MUST equal the MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK value in the consensus layer configuration.

state_variables.name: BLOB_SCHEDULE
state_variables.description: Consensus layer configuration field containing blob parameter change entries after ELECTRA_FORK_EPOCH.

data_structures.name: CL BLOB_SCHEDULE YAML
data_structures.description: Consensus layer configuration for blob schedule with EPOCH and MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK per entry.

sub_graphs.name: Modified compute_fork_digest
sub_graphs.description: Updates the compute_fork_digest helper to account for BPO forks by XOR-bitmasking the max_blobs_per_block parameter into the base 4-byte fork digest. This ensures that peers on different blob schedules produce different fork digests, enabling correct peer discovery and gossip topic rotation.

invariants.text: max_blobs_per_block MUST fit within a 32-bit unsigned integer (0 <= max_blobs_per_block <= 0xFFFFFFFF).
If no blob schedule entry applies to the current epoch (blob_params is None), the base digest is returned unchanged.

functions.signature: def compute_fork_digest(current_version: Version, genesis_validators_root: Root, current_epoch: Epoch, blob_schedule: Sequence[BlobScheduleEntry]) -> ForkDigest

parameters.name: current_version
parameters.description: The baseline hardfork version atop which the blob schedule is applied (unchanged from original).

parameters.name: genesis_validators_root

parameters.name: current_epoch
parameters.description: The current epoch used to look up the applicable blob schedule entry (new parameter).

parameters.name: blob_schedule
parameters.description: The full blob schedule sequence to determine current blob parameters (new parameter).

functions.description: Returns the 4-byte fork digest for the current_version and genesis_validators_root, bitmasking blob parameters after ELECTRA_FORK_VERSION. The function computes the base digest, finds the applicable blob schedule entry for the current epoch, and XORs max_blobs_per_block (as 4 big-endian bytes) into the base digest.

state_transitions.description: When no blob schedule entry applies (blob_params is None), the base digest (4 bytes from compute_fork_data_root) is returned directly.
state_transitions.from_state: No applicable blob schedule for current_epoch

state_transitions.description: When a blob schedule entry applies, the digest is XOR-masked with max_blobs_per_block encoded as 4 big-endian bytes.

data_structures.name: BlobScheduleEntry

preconditions.text: current_version must be a valid fork version identifier.
genesis_validators_root must be the correct root for the chain.
blob_schedule entries must have unique, valid epoch values.

postconditions.text: The returned ForkDigest is exactly 4 bytes.
Two nodes with identical blob schedules and same current_epoch produce the same fork digest.
Nodes on different blob schedule entries (different max_blobs_per_block) produce different fork digests (with overwhelming probability).

sub_graphs.name: P2P Networking: ENR Extension
sub_graphs.description: Extends consensus layer ENRs (Ethereum Node Records) with a new 'nfd' (next fork digest) field that communicates the digest of the next scheduled fork, whether regular or BPO. This is agnostic to specific fork types and offers long-term flexibility for peer discovery.

invariants.text: When discovering and interfacing with peers, nodes MUST evaluate 'nfd' alongside their existing consideration of the ENRForkID::next_* fields under the 'eth2' key.

state_variables.name: nfd
state_variables.description: ENR key 'nfd' (next fork digest): communicates the digest of the next scheduled fork in the consensus layer ENR.

sub_graphs.name: P2P Networking: Status and Gossip
sub_graphs.description: Clarifies that no changes are needed to the Status req/resp interaction (though the response payload must correctly contain the updated fork_digest). No changes are required to gossip topic structure or configuration; however, all topics automatically rotate at a BPO fork due to changes in their ForkDigestValue component.

invariants.text: The Status response payload must correctly contain the updated fork_digest after a BPO fork.
All gossip topics automatically rotate at a BPO fork due to changes in their ForkDigestValue component.

sub_graphs.name: Cross-Layer Consistency Requirements
sub_graphs.description: Defines the critical consistency constraints between execution layer and consensus layer BPO configurations, ensuring that both layers agree on fork schedules, activation times, and blob limits.

invariants.text: Execution and consensus clients MUST share consistent BPO fork schedules.
The slot number in the EL's blobSchedule MUST align with the start of the epoch specified in the consensus layer configuration.
The 'max' field in the EL's blobSchedule MUST equal the MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK value in the consensus layer configuration.

preconditions.text: Both EL and CL clients must be configured with the same set of BPO fork entries before activation.

postconditions.text: At any given time, the blob parameters in effect on the EL match those in effect on the CL.

metadata.backwards_compatibility: BPO forks introduce no backwards compatibility concerns.
metadata.security_considerations: No security risks have been identified.

sub_graphs.name: BeaconState Extension: Proposer Lookahead Field
sub_graphs.description: Extends the BeaconState container with a new 'proposer_lookahead' field. This field is a fixed-size vector of ValidatorIndex values covering the full visible lookahead period, from the start of the current epoch through the next MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD epochs. The vector length is (MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1) * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH. For example, proposer_lookahead[0] is the proposer for the first slot of the current epoch, and proposer_lookahead[SLOTS_PER_EPOCH + 4] is the proposer for the fifth slot of the next epoch.

invariants.text: The proposer_lookahead vector MUST always have exactly (MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1) * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH entries.
proposer_lookahead[0] MUST correspond to the validator index of the proposer for the first slot of the current epoch.
Each entry in proposer_lookahead MUST be a valid ValidatorIndex referencing an active validator eligible for proposing in the corresponding epoch.
proposer_lookahead[SLOTS_PER_EPOCH + k] MUST be the validator index for slot k of the next epoch (for k in 0..SLOTS_PER_EPOCH-1).

state_variables.name: proposer_lookahead
state_variables.description: A fixed-size vector storing pre-computed proposer validator indices for the current epoch and the next MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD epochs. Indexed positionally so that index i maps to the (i % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH)-th slot of epoch (current_epoch + i // SLOTS_PER_EPOCH).

data_structures.name: BeaconState (extended)
data_structures.description: The BeaconState container is extended with a proposer_lookahead field appended to the existing fields.

constants_referenced.name: MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD
constants_referenced.description: The minimum number of epochs of seed lookahead. Determines how far ahead the proposer schedule is pre-computed.

constants_referenced.name: SLOTS_PER_EPOCH
constants_referenced.description: Number of slots in each epoch. Determines the size of each epoch chunk in the lookahead vector.

sub_graphs.name: Proposer Index Lookup (get_beacon_proposer_index)
sub_graphs.description: Replaces the previous on-demand calculation of the beacon proposer index with a simple O(1) lookup into the pre-computed proposer_lookahead vector. Uses (state.slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH) as the index into the vector, returning the proposer for the current slot in constant time.

invariants.text: get_beacon_proposer_index MUST return a valid ValidatorIndex for every slot within the current epoch.
The returned index MUST correspond to an active validator eligible for proposing at the given slot.
The function MUST be deterministic: for the same state and slot, it MUST always return the same ValidatorIndex.
The function is read-only: it MUST NOT modify any state.

functions.name: get_beacon_proposer_index

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The current beacon chain state containing the proposer_lookahead vector.

functions.description: Return the beacon proposer index at the current slot by performing a direct lookup into state.proposer_lookahead using state.slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH as the index.
functions.source:
def get_beacon_proposer_index(state: BeaconState) -> ValidatorIndex:
    """
    Return the beacon proposer index at the current slot.
    """
    return state.proposer_lookahead[state.slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH]

preconditions.text: state.proposer_lookahead MUST have been initialized (either at fork or during epoch processing).
state.slot MUST be within a valid epoch range covered by the lookahead.

postconditions.text: Returns the ValidatorIndex of the proposer for the current slot without modifying any state.

sub_graphs.name: Epoch Boundary Processing (process_proposer_lookahead)
sub_graphs.description: At each epoch boundary, the proposer_lookahead vector is updated by shifting out the expired (current) epoch's entries and appending newly computed proposer indices for the epoch that is MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1 ahead. This is called as part of process_epoch, ensuring the lookahead always covers the required forward window.

invariants.text: After process_proposer_lookahead completes, the vector MUST contain valid proposer indices for exactly (MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1) epochs starting from the new current epoch.
The proposer indices for the overlapping epochs (those not shifted out) MUST remain unchanged after the shift operation.
The newly appended epoch's proposer indices MUST be computed using the RANDAO seed for epoch (current_epoch + MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1) and the effective balances at the time of the epoch transition.

functions.name: process_epoch
functions.description: Top-level epoch processing function. Modified to include a call to process_proposer_lookahead(state) as part of epoch boundary processing.

functions.name: process_proposer_lookahead
functions.description: Performs the epoch-boundary update of the proposer_lookahead vector. Computes last_epoch_start as len(proposer_lookahead) - SLOTS_PER_EPOCH, then shifts proposer_lookahead[:last_epoch_start] = proposer_lookahead[SLOTS_PER_EPOCH:] to remove the expired epoch. Then computes new proposer indices for epoch (current_epoch + MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1) and writes them into proposer_lookahead[last_epoch_start:].
functions.source:
def process_proposer_lookahead(state: BeaconState) -> None:
    last_epoch_start = len(state.proposer_lookahead) - SLOTS_PER_EPOCH
    # Shift out proposers in the first epoch
    state.proposer_lookahead[:last_epoch_start] = state.proposer_lookahead[SLOTS_PER_EPOCH:]
    # Fill in the last epoch with new proposer indices
    last_epoch_proposers = get_beacon_proposer_indices(
        state, Epoch(get_current_epoch(state) + MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1)
    )
    state.proposer_lookahead[last_epoch_start:] = last_epoch_proposers
functions.complexity: O(SLOTS_PER_EPOCH * V) where V is the number of active validators (due to proposer election sampling)

state_transitions.description: Shifts the proposer_lookahead vector forward by one epoch and appends freshly computed proposers for the newly visible future epoch.

preconditions.text: This function MUST be called during epoch processing (process_epoch), after all other state updates that could affect effective balances have been applied for the current epoch.
The RANDAO seed for the target epoch (current_epoch + MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1) MUST be deterministically derivable from the current state.

postconditions.text: state.proposer_lookahead[0:last_epoch_start] contains the shifted-forward proposer indices from the previous lookahead.
state.proposer_lookahead[last_epoch_start:] contains freshly computed proposer indices for the newly visible epoch.

sub_graphs.name: Proposer Index Computation (get_beacon_proposer_indices / compute_proposer_indices)
sub_graphs.description: Computes the full vector of proposer indices for a given epoch. This involves fetching active validator indices and the RANDAO seed for the target epoch, then deriving per-slot seeds by hashing the epoch seed concatenated with each slot number, and selecting a proposer for each slot using the existing compute_proposer_index function.

invariants.text: The returned vector MUST have exactly SLOTS_PER_EPOCH entries, one proposer index per slot in the target epoch.
Each proposer index MUST reference a validator that is active in the target epoch.
The computation MUST be deterministic: given the same state (effective balances and RANDAO), the same proposer schedule MUST be produced.
The per-slot seed is derived as hash(epoch_seed + uint_to_bytes(start_slot + i)) for slot i in the epoch.

functions.name: get_beacon_proposer_indices
functions.signature: get_beacon_proposer_indices(state: BeaconState, epoch: Epoch) -> Vector[ValidatorIndex, SLOTS_PER_EPOCH]

parameters.name: epoch
parameters.description: The target epoch for which to compute proposer indices.

functions.description: Returns the proposer indices for the given epoch by: (1) fetching active validator indices via get_active_validator_indices(state, epoch), (2) obtaining the seed via get_seed(state, epoch, DOMAIN_BEACON_PROPOSER), and (3) delegating to compute_proposer_indices.

functions.name: compute_proposer_indices
functions.signature: compute_proposer_indices(state: BeaconState, epoch: Epoch, seed: Bytes32, indices: Sequence[ValidatorIndex]) -> Vector[ValidatorIndex, SLOTS_PER_EPOCH]

parameters.name: seed
parameters.description: The epoch-level RANDAO seed used for proposer selection.

parameters.name: indices
parameters.description: Active validator indices for the target epoch.

functions.description: Computes a per-slot seed for each of the SLOTS_PER_EPOCH slots in the target epoch by hashing the epoch seed concatenated with the slot number (as bytes). Then for each per-slot seed, calls compute_proposer_index to select the proposer. Returns the full vector of proposer indices.
functions.source:
def compute_proposer_indices(
    state: BeaconState, epoch: Epoch, seed: Bytes32, indices: Sequence[ValidatorIndex]
) -> Vector[ValidatorIndex, SLOTS_PER_EPOCH]:
    """
    Return the proposer indices for the given ``epoch``.
    """
    start_slot = compute_start_slot_at_epoch(epoch)
    seeds = [hash(seed + uint_to_bytes(Slot(start_slot + i))) for i in range(SLOTS_PER_EPOCH)]
    return [compute_proposer_index(state, indices, seed) for seed in seeds]

preconditions.text: The epoch MUST be within the range for which seeds are available in the state (the RANDAO mix for the target epoch must exist).
The set of active validators for the target epoch MUST be non-empty.

postconditions.text: Returns a Vector[ValidatorIndex, SLOTS_PER_EPOCH] containing exactly one proposer per slot for the given epoch.

sub_graphs.name: Fork Initialization of Proposer Lookahead
sub_graphs.description: The first block after the Fulu fork activation MUST calculate all lookaheads for epochs up to MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD ahead and fill the proposer_lookahead field in the beacon state. This is a one-time initialization that bootstraps the lookahead vector from an empty/default state to a fully populated schedule.

invariants.text: After fork initialization, the proposer_lookahead vector MUST be fully populated with valid proposer indices for (MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1) epochs.
The fork initialization MUST produce the same lookahead values that would have been computed if the mechanism had been active from genesis with the same RANDAO seeds and effective balances.

preconditions.text: The Fulu fork has been activated (the chain has transitioned to the Fulu fork).
The proposer_lookahead field exists in the BeaconState (default-initialized to zeros or empty).

postconditions.text: state.proposer_lookahead is fully populated with (MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1) * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH valid proposer indices covering from the current epoch through current_epoch + MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD.

state_transitions.description: On the first block after the Fulu fork, the proposer_lookahead vector is bootstrapped from default state to fully populated.
state_transitions.from_state: proposer_lookahead is default-initialized (all zeros or empty)
state_transitions.to_state: proposer_lookahead is fully populated for current epoch through current_epoch + MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD

sub_graphs.name: Security: Effective Balance Grinding Prevention
sub_graphs.description: By computing the proposer lookahead at the epoch boundary using effective balances frozen at the start of epoch N - MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD (rather than the start of epoch N), this EIP removes the ability for validators to manipulate their effective balance after seeing the RANDAO outcome to influence the proposer schedule. This aligns the effective-balance delay with the RANDAO delay, collapsing the security analysis from a subtle examination of EB edge cases to a trivial analysis.

invariants.text: The proposer schedule for epoch N MUST be determined entirely by the RANDAO seed from epoch N - MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD - 1 and the effective balances at the start of epoch N - MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD.
No action taken by a validator after the start of epoch N - MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD can alter the proposer schedule for epoch N.
The RANDAO delay and the effective-balance delay for proposer election are aligned, both being MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD epochs.

security_properties.name: Effective Balance Grinding Resistance
security_properties.description: Validators cannot adjust effective balance after seeing RANDAO to influence the proposer schedule. Before this EIP, effective balances for epoch N's proposer schedule were taken at the start of epoch N, while the RANDAO seed was known at epoch N - MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD. This created a window where a validator could grind EB to manipulate the schedule. Now both inputs are frozen at epoch N - MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD.
security_properties.attack_vector: A validator observes the RANDAO seed for a future epoch and manipulates their effective balance (via slashings, penalties accumulating to >= 1 ETH, consolidations, deposits, or reward accumulation beyond 32 ETH with EIP-7251) to increase their probability of being selected as proposer.
security_properties.mitigation: Effective balances used for proposer election are frozen at the same time as the RANDAO seed, eliminating the grinding window entirely.

security_properties.name: EIP-7251 (MaxEB) Interaction
security_properties.description: EIP-7251 increases effective balance unpredictability by allowing EBs to exceed 32 ETH through rewards accumulating to >= 1 ETH, validator consolidations, and deposits. This EIP mitigates the increased attack surface by freezing EBs earlier in the proposer election pipeline.
security_properties.attack_vector: With uncapped MaxEB, more frequent effective balance changes (rewards crossing 1 ETH thresholds, validator consolidations) create additional opportunities for proposer schedule manipulation.
security_properties.mitigation: The deterministic lookahead pre-computes the schedule before any EB changes can take effect.

security_properties.name: RANDAO and EB Delay Alignment
security_properties.description: Before this EIP, the RANDAO delay and EB delay were misaligned: the RANDAO seed for epoch N was fixed at epoch N - MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD - 1, but EBs could change up to the start of epoch N. By aligning both to the same point in time, the possibility of validators adjusting EB after seeing the RANDAO outcome is removed entirely, simplifying security analysis.
security_properties.attack_vector: Validators could observe the fixed RANDAO seed and then manipulate their EB within the remaining window before the proposer schedule calculation.
security_properties.mitigation: Both RANDAO seeds and effective balances are now fixed at the same epoch boundary, eliminating the manipulation window.

sub_graphs.name: Application Layer Accessibility via Beacon Root
sub_graphs.description: The proposer_lookahead field being stored in the BeaconState makes the next-epoch proposer schedule accessible to the EVM application layer via the beacon state root and a simple Merkle proof. This highly simplifies the implementation of on-chain components for based preconfirmation protocols, which previously required off-chain oracles or complex attestation mechanisms.

invariants.text: The proposer_lookahead MUST be part of the BeaconState Merkle tree, making it provable via the beacon state root.
The proposer schedule for the next epoch MUST be fully deterministic and verifiable from any beacon state within the current epoch.

preconditions.text: The beacon root MUST be accessible from the execution layer (as provided by EIP-4788).

postconditions.text: Smart contracts can verify the proposer for any slot in the lookahead window using a Merkle proof against the beacon state root.

use_cases.name: Based Preconfirmation Protocols
use_cases.description: On-chain components of based preconfirmation protocols can read and verify the upcoming proposer schedule directly from the beacon state via Merkle proofs, rather than relying on off-chain attestations or oracles. This highly simplifies implementation.

use_cases.name: CL Client Ahead-of-Time Visibility
use_cases.description: Consensus layer clients gain ahead-of-time visibility over the next proposer, which may simplify implementations for block production, attestation, and sync committee duties.

sub_graphs.name: SSLE Forward Compatibility
sub_graphs.description: The proposer_lookahead field is designed to be forward-compatible with future Single Secret Leader Election (SSLE) mechanisms. Current SSLE designs still rely on a lookahead, albeit an encrypted one. The field type could be changed to store encrypted validator indices (e.g. List[EncryptedValidatorIndex]). If a future construction removes lookahead entirely, the field can be set to an empty list.

invariants.text: The proposer_lookahead field type can be adapted for encrypted indices in future SSLE implementations without introducing backwards-incompatible changes beyond what a fork upgrade would require.

sub_graphs.design_rationale: Current SSLE designs still rely on a lookahead, albeit encrypted. The proposer_lookahead field can be reused by changing its type to List[EncryptedValidatorIndex]. If a construction removes lookahead entirely, the field can be set to an empty list. APS (Attester Proposer Separation) envisions more sophisticated (i.e., more DDoS-resistant) execution proposers, reducing the need for SSLE.

sub_graphs.name: Performance: Added Computation at Epoch Boundary
sub_graphs.description: Before this EIP, consensus clients only needed to compute the current proposer's index at each slot. With this EIP, they must calculate the entire epoch's proposer schedule (SLOTS_PER_EPOCH proposer elections) at the start of each epoch. Computing the proposer index is light, involving sampling validators until a validator with sufficient effective balance is selected. However, testing is needed to confirm no performance bottlenecks.

invariants.text: The epoch boundary computation MUST complete within acceptable time bounds to avoid delaying epoch processing.

performance_considerations.before: Proposer index computed on-demand at each slot (1 computation per slot).
performance_considerations.after: Full epoch proposer schedule (SLOTS_PER_EPOCH computations) calculated at each epoch boundary, with O(1) lookups per slot.
performance_considerations.tradeoff: Batch computation at epoch boundary replaces per-slot computation. Each individual proposer election is lightweight (sampling validators until sufficient EB is found), but SLOTS_PER_EPOCH (32) such elections occur at once.
performance_considerations.testing_required: Testing needed to confirm that the additional epoch-boundary calculations do not create performance bottlenecks in practice.

cross_references.description: get_beacon_proposer_index reads from the proposer_lookahead state variable defined in SG-001.
process_proposer_lookahead modifies the proposer_lookahead state variable defined in SG-001.
process_proposer_lookahead calls get_beacon_proposer_indices to compute the new epoch's proposer schedule.
get_beacon_proposer_indices delegates to compute_proposer_indices for the actual per-slot computation.
Fork initialization uses the same proposer index computation functions from SG-004 to bootstrap the lookahead.
The EB grinding prevention (SG-006) is enforced by the timing of when process_proposer_lookahead (SG-003) computes and freezes the proposer schedule.
Application layer accessibility depends on proposer_lookahead being a field in BeaconState (SG-001) to be Merkle-provable.
The added epoch boundary computation cost (SG-009) is a direct consequence of the batch schedule computation in process_proposer_lookahead (SG-003).

external_dependencies.name: EIP-7251 (MaxEB / Increase Max Effective Balance)
external_dependencies.description: EIP-7251 increases effective balance unpredictability (EBs can now exceed 32 ETH), which was a key motivation for introducing deterministic proposer lookahead to prevent EB grinding.

external_dependencies.name: EIP-4788 (Beacon Block Root in the EVM)
external_dependencies.description: EIP-4788 provides the mechanism by which the beacon state root (and thus the proposer_lookahead) is accessible from the EVM execution layer for Merkle proof verification.

external_dependencies.name: Fulu Fork (Consensus Specs)
external_dependencies.description: This EIP is activated as part of the Fulu fork. The consensus-specs define the complete implementation details including fork initialization logic.

external_dependencies.name: RANDAO (Beacon Chain Randomness)
external_dependencies.description: The proposer election relies on RANDAO seeds which have a deterministic lookahead of at least MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD == 1 epoch. The RANDAO delay is unchanged by this EIP.

external_dependencies.name: compute_proposer_index (Existing Beacon Chain Function)
external_dependencies.description: The per-slot proposer selection still uses the existing compute_proposer_index function, which samples validators weighted by effective balance.

metadata.security_considerations: This proposal does not increase the chances of malicious lookahead alteration. The RANDAO delay is unchanged. The only difference is the effective-balance delay: rather than using EB at the start of epoch N, it uses EB at the start of epoch N - MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD. This removes the possibility of EB grinding after seeing the RANDAO outcome.
